steps.text: Combine basil, Parmesan cheese, olive oil, pine nuts, and garlic in the bowl of a food processor or blender. Blend to a smooth paste. Add lemon juice, if desired, and quickly pulse to combine.

raw_recipe.headline: Pesto
raw_recipe.description: This basic pesto is a no-fail recipe made with aromatic basil, olive oil, garlic, Parmesan, pine nuts, and parsley. Great as a dip, spread, or sauce.

video.description: In this video, Nicole shows you how to make basil pesto with fresh basil leaves and parmesan cheese. This recipe only uses a few ingredients and is super easy-to-make. Using a food processor, pulse together the basil leaves, garlic cloves, pine nuts, parmesan cheese, and olive oil. Then, transfer to a food container. For a fast and easy dinner, use the pesto for a bowl of pasta or as a spread for your bread!
video.name: How to Make Basil Pesto

raw_recipe.name: Pesto

recipeInstructions.text: Combine basil, Parmesan cheese, olive oil, pine nuts, and garlic in the bowl of a food processor or blender. Blend to a smooth paste. Add lemon juice, if desired, and quickly pulse to combine.

review.reviewBody: Perfect pesto! Don't forget to toast the pine nuts, it makes all the difference...just put them in a small frying pan on the stove and toss them around until they start to turn brown. Don't worry about toasting all sides, just wing it!

VERY GOOD, and easy. A full flavor Pesto for sure. I added a smidge of coarse salt, and froze it in ice cube trays. After frozen I popped it out (with the help of a fork), and keep the cubes in the freezer. Talk about a FAST side dish. Pasta, a cube of defrosted Pesto, a diced fresh tomato, and it's a meal!! Thanks for a GREAT basic recipe!

This is it! Real, authentic pesto. I made several batches this morning with our fresh garden basil and my son was in pesto heaven! If you are making and freezing one-cup batches as I am, then cover the top of each container with a thin layer of olive oil. Basil tends to turn brown when exposed to air. When you thaw the container, the basil won't turn color. Use the best Extra Virgin Olive Oil you can afford! Thanks for the great recipe!

This is a good recipe. The only suggestion I have is to add some lemon juice to the pesto or store it in the refrigerator with a thin layer of olive oil on the top. Otherwise, the top of the pesto turns black.

i love garlic, but i agree that using 2 vs 4 cloves keeps the flavors more balanced. for those wanting to freeze but mentioned it was messy to do so, freezing in silicone ice cube trays makes it easy to pop them out vs a hard tray ;-)

This recipe is very good. I made half a recipe for storage and freshness purposes. I did follow the suggestion of many about reducing the garlic and using a pinch of coarse salt. It was perfect in every possible way. I think is a great idea the suggestion of scooping little balls with a melon scooper to then freeze instead of freezing in ice trays. For those watching portions it is the best idea to keep track of them. Will make it again!

Made this recipe exactly as prescribed except used Sliced almonds in place of pinenuts and a quarter teaspoon sea salt. Also I did roast the almonds in a dry, small frying pan over Medium heat. it can be stored in the refrigerator in a pint jar with olive oil over the top to keep it from going black .

Great taste and very easy to prepare. I place the pesto in a clean dry ice cube tray and freeze for about 2 hours then I pop them out and wrap each in Saran and place them in a freezer zip lock bag for future use. I found this recipe will fill a 12 ice cube tray with some left over.

Quite good with following changes: 1.5 cups spinach leaves packed, 3 cups packed basil, 1/2 tsp garlic, 1/2 c. olive oil, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/3 c. parmesan, 1/4 c. almonds. Makes 1.5 cups pesto...

*Try: Doubling spinach (3 cups instead of 1.5 cups). May need to add more sauce when doing so (oil, salt, cheese, garlic powder, almonds). Or could try the Spinach Basil pesto recipe.
*Can make it without spinach, still good, but better with it.

I substitute walnuts, toasted, for the pine nuts as I always have walnuts on hand. Other than that, I follow the directions exactly, including the parsley. It is amazing! I freeze it in cubes and have 'fresh' basil flavor all year.
Yummy! I used two cloves, juice of one lemon, handful of almonds, 1/2 cup parm, 1/2 cup olive oil, salt/pepper and tons of basil packed in my nutrabullet. Easy and wonderful!

Wonderful everytime! two things to share: first, I love garlic but 4 cloves might be a bit too strong depending on the type of garlic.; second, if you are goint to freeze your pesto (i use the icecube tray method) I find that it's better to leave the cheese out and add it in after you thaw your frozen stash. Peace.
Easy and delicious. I used walnuts instead of pine nuts.
I substituted walnuts and recipe came out great. Easy to make and tastes wonderful.

Classic Pesto Recipe. Easy to mix up and the taste is amazing. I use a little less garlic and substitute almonds for the pine nuts. I spread the pesto on wheat thins for a snack. It's also delicious on pasta.
Great recipe. I always use walnuts, a half lemon(lemon zest too sometimes) and some water to cut down the oil in my pesto.
perfect measures.

I interpreted the cups of "packed" basil just that .... packed. Unfortunately I "packed" too much basil. It was pretty bitter. So, I started adding more of the other ingredients to try and balance it out. Even with this being a larger batch, 4 cloves of garlic was too much for my taste. I'll make some modifications next time.
I dont spend the $$ on Pine Nuts and replace with unsalted peanuts, works well! Outstanding results!😉👍🇨🇦
Good recipe. Might need salt/pepper
